| [NOTE-052](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-052.md) v2 | Consciousness in AI: indicator properties | The report assumes computational functionalism and takes a "theory-heavy" approach. From it the authors derive 14 indicator properties: RPT-1–2, GWT-1–4, HOT-1–4, AST-1, PP-1 and AE-1–2. The claim for them is only that more of them raises the probability of consciousness. They assess a handful of systems against subsets of the list and conclude that no current system "appears to be a strong candidate". Transformer LLMs have "only a relatively weak case" for any GWT indicator, because a single forward pass has no recurrence or global broadcast. Perceiver arguably has GWT-1, GWT-2 and half of GWT-4 but lacks broadcast. Among the embodied agents, AdA is the likeliest to meet AE-2. Most indicators could be built with standard ML techniques. The abstract's "no current AI systems are conscious" is stronger than anything the body shows. | Read |
| [NOTE-081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-081.md) v2 | The No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) | NUTS removes HMC's step-count L. It doubles a leapfrog trajectory forwards and backwards in random directions until some balanced subtree satisfies (θ⁺−θ⁻)·r⁻ < 0 or (θ⁺−θ⁻)·r⁺ < 0. With uniform features the directions settle into uniform polytopes, with feature dimensionalities clustering at 3/4, 2/3, 1/2, 2/5 and 3/8. In pre-grokking (to ~10⁵ steps) training accuracy saturates while test accuracy stays low. In grokking (~10⁵–10⁶) test accuracy rises to ~0.85. The paper's own weight-decay control shows FC2's α below 2, and traps in both layers, *without* a collapse (Fig. 6, Table 2). That undercuts its headline claim that α < 2 "invariably" heralds collapse. | Read |

Learned matching mainly refines O. Small models only. | Read |
| [NOTE-541](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-541.md) | Intermediate Layer Classifiers for OOD generalization | ILC_l(x) = W_l r_l(x) + b_l on frozen layer-l features, l ≤ L − 2, layer chosen on OOD validation data. Few-shot, best ILC minus last-layer retraining: +16.8, +6.3, +1.6, +6.3 points (ResNets on CMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100C, MultiCelebA); +27.0 on MultiCelebA at π ≤ 0.03. Zero-shot worst-group accuracy: Waterbirds 79.4 → 87.1, CelebA 56.0 → 82.0, MultiCelebA 20.8 → 46.0. Layer 7 beats 8 everywhere in Figure 8. Intermediate features are less displaced by shift for minority groups. | Read |
| [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md) | Rethinking generalization requires revisiting old ideas: statistical mechanics approaches and complex learning behavior | VSDL model: f = f(x; α, τ), α = m_eff/N lowered by label noise, τ raised by early stopping. Thermodynamic limit m, N → ∞ with α = m/N fixed. Continuous perceptron: s(ε) ~ ln ε, so 1/ε − α = 0 gives ε ~ 1/α (Eqs. 6–8). Ising perceptron: s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, and −π²ε ln ε = α has no solution for large α, so ε falls discontinuously to 0 at αc (Eqs. 9–13). Rigorous bound: error ≤ ε* + ε_τ, ε* the rightmost crossing of s(ε) and −α log(1 − ε) (Eqs. 14–18). No new theorem, no experiment. | Read |
| [NOTE-543](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-543.md) | Proving Linear Mode Connectivity of Neural Networks via Optimal Transport | Layerwise neuron alignment equals a Wasserstein distance between empirical weight distributions (Birkhoff), so LMC modulo permutation follows when neuron weights are i.i.d. and layers are wide: for mean-field two-layer SGD (Theorem 3.1), and for deep Gaussian or sub-Gaussian nets with m̃_ℓ = Õ((T_ℓ/ε)^{m̃_{ℓ−1}}) (Theorem 5.2), tight by Theorem 5.3. Low-dimensional weights relax this (Theorem 5.4). | Read |
| [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md) | Explaining Landscape Connectivity of Low-cost Solutions for Multilayer Nets | ε-dropout-stable ReLU nets are ε-connected by a piecewise-linear path (Theorem 1); ε-noise-stable nets by 10 segments with barrier Õ(ε) (Theorem 2), or 13 through a narrow low-loss net (Theorem 3). For any width there is a teacher dataset on which a two-layer student's global minima are disconnected (Theorem 4). MNIST convnets and a VGG-11 on CIFAR-10 satisfy the conditions roughly. | Read |
| [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md) | Conditional Simulation Using Diffusion Schrödinger Bridges | Posterior sampling p(x\|y) when only joint samples (X, Y) can be drawn, recast as a Schrödinger bridge on the extended space between the joint p(x, y) and a reference p_ref(x\|y)p(y) in which y is held fixed (Proposition 1), and solved by iterative proportional fitting with learned forward and backward drifts (CDSB). Its first iteration is the ordinary conditional score-based model, so the rest refine it; the reference can be an informed guess (upsampled image, EnKF, SRFlow) rather than noise. Better than the conditional score model at equal, small numbers of steps on most but not all image metrics, and it filters Lorenz-63 with 20 steps where the score model diverges. | Read |
| [NOTE-592](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-592.md) | T2I-CompBench | 6,000 compositional prompts (attribute binding by colour, shape and texture; spatial and non-spatial relations; complex), each sub-category split 700/300, with a metric per category: question-per-object BLIP-VQA for binding (Kendall τ 0.63 with humans on colour against 0.19 for CLIPScore), a UniDet box rule for space, and a 3-in-1 average for complex prompts. Spatial relations are hardest. GORS, reward-weighted LoRA finetuning of SD v2 on its own selected samples, is rated best by humans in every sub-category, but its binding score falls sharply on pairs unseen in finetuning. | Read |
| [NOTE-593](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-593.md) | GenEval | An automated text-to-image benchmark of 553 templated prompts in six tasks, scored per image as correct or not by a COCO-trained Mask2Former (presence, count, position) and masked-crop zero-shot CLIP (colour). 83% agreement with human annotators against 88% between annotators, and 91% on unanimous images; beats a per-task tuned CLIPScore on counting, position and binding. Best 2023 open model (IF-XL) scores 0.61 overall, at most 0.15 on position and 0.35 on attribute binding. | Read |
| [NOTE-597](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-597.md) | Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models | Treats a conditional diffusion model's noise prediction as the gradient of an energy, so concepts compose at sampling time by adding scores: AND is ε(x,t) + Σ wᵢ(ε(x,t\|cᵢ) − ε(x,t)), the product p(x)Πp(x\|cᵢ)/p(x) under conditional independence of the concepts given x; NOT divides by the negated concept's likelihood. No retraining. On CLEVR object positions it beats an EBM baseline (31.36% against 7.34% at three components); on relations it does not (2.80% against 4.26%); on FFHQ attributes it trails LACE in accuracy at three components but has the best FID. Text composition with GLIDE and Stable Diffusion is qualitative only. | Read |
| [NOTE-607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-607.md) | Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations | Shows empirically that the correctness of in-context labels contributes little to classification and multi-choice accuracy, while the input distribution, the label space and the paired format contribute most of the gain over zero-shot. The authors read this as the demonstrations locating a correspondence the model already has, not teaching a new one. | Read |
| [NOTE-610](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-610.md) | T2I-CompBench++ | Extends T2I-CompBench to eight sub-categories (adding numeracy and 3D spatial relations), tests multimodal LLMs as judges, and benchmarks eleven models. GPT-4V agrees with human rankings best on interactions and complex prompts, where CLIPScore and the conference version's 3-in-1 metric were weak; specialised VQA and detector metrics stay best elsewhere. Human ratings cover only six 2023-era models, and the interaction category remains near ceiling for humans. | Read |
| [NOTE-620](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-620.md) | Learning to (Learn at Test Time) | Recasts a sequence-modelling layer as a learner trained on the sequence it reads: hidden state as inner-model weights, update as a gradient step on a learned self-supervised loss. Proves that the linear, batch-GD case is linear attention and that a Nadaraya–Watson inner learner is softmax attention; shows TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP use long context better than Mamba at up to 1.3B parameters. | Read |
| [NOTE-625](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-625.md) | Backprop as Functor | Learners (P, I, U, r), with a request function r : P × A × B → A, compose and form a symmetric monoidal category Learn. For step size ε and an error e with ∂e/∂x(x₀, −) invertible, sending a differentiable parametrised function to (P, I, p − ε∇ₚE, f_a(∇ₐE)) is a faithful strong symmetric monoidal functor Para → Learn: gradient descent on a composite is the composite of local updates exchanging requests, which is backpropagation, and the proof is the chain rule. | Read |
| [NOTE-626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-626.md) | Fantastically Ordered Prompts | Shows that permuting a fixed set of few-shot examples swings GPT-family accuracy from near chance to near state of the art, at every model size tested, with good orders uncorrelated across sizes and the variance surviving more examples and calibration; proposes ranking orders by the label entropy they induce on a probing set the model generates itself. | Read |
| [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) | Implicit Bayesian inference account of in-context learning | Proves that if pretraining text is a mixture of HMMs and a model fits it exactly, conditioning on a prompt of concatenated examples recovers the prompt's latent concept by posterior concentration, and the in-context predictor is asymptotically Bayes-optimal, whenever each example's KL signal about the concept beats the error from the improbable transitions between examples. The account is of the data distribution, not of any network's computation. | Read |
| [NOTE-639](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-639.md) | Attend-and-Excite | Identifies catastrophic neglect in Stable Diffusion, where a named subject never appears because no image patch attends to its token, and corrects it at inference by gradient steps on the latent that raise the smoothed peak attention of the most neglected subject token during the early steps. Measured gains are in CLIP and caption similarity and human preference on two-subject prompts; attribute binding improves only in the figures, and relations are not addressed. | Read |
| [NOTE-648](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-648.md) | Quantum-Like Contextuality in Large Language Models | Builds a three-sentence anaphora schema with the support of the PR prism, instantiates it 51,966,480 times from Simple English Wikipedia, and takes one referent probability per sentence from BERT: 0.148% of the models pass a signalling-corrected sheaf test and 71.1% the CbD test. Because the schema fixes the support, both verdicts depend only on how uncertain BERT is in the three sentences; the tie to embedding distance is a softmax identity with weak correlations. | Read |
| [NOTE-649](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-649.md) | Large AI models are cultural and social technologies | Argues that large models are a cultural and social technology, not intelligent agents: lossy, uninvertible summaries of human-produced corpora that, like prices and bureaucratic categories, allow the information to be reorganized at scale. The argument is by analogy and classification; no evidence is offered that could have come out otherwise. It names one mechanism (fitting the training distribution on average makes models worst where data are rare, which may homogenize culture) and leaves both it and its remedy untested. | Read |
| [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md) | Relative representations enable zero-shot latent space communication | Represents each sample by its cosine similarities to a fixed set of anchor samples. That vector is invariant by construction to every cosine-preserving map of the latent space (rotations, reflections, global and even per-sample positive rescaling), not to translations or general linear maps. With anchors matched across encoders it lets a decoder trained on one encoder run untrained on another, across seeds, architectures, latent sizes and languages: far better than raw latents, but with large and uneven losses. The assumption that such spaces differ by an angle-preserving map is never tested directly, and the evidence supports it only approximately. | Read |
| [NOTE-653](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-653.md) | Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations | An empirical paper with no theorems. It defines the stitching penalty, the change in a top network's test error when its bottom ℓ layers are replaced by another representation through a trained 1×1 convolution, and uses it to show, in single runs mostly on CIFAR-10, that networks from different seeds, and supervised and self-supervised ImageNet networks, are interchangeable layer by layer where CKA calls them different, and that a bottom trained on more data improves a weaker top. The ordering it gives is by one task's loss through a fixed head and a restricted map class, which is not an ordering by information. | Read |
| [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md) v2 | Exact Learning Dynamics of In-Context Learning in Linear Transformers | Solves the averaged gradient-flow dynamics of one linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression, when tasks and input covariance share an eigenbasis and the weights are assumed to stay in it: each mode is a logistic curve on timescale (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, so learning is staged by the input spectrum, and the fixed point is the known preconditioned predictor W Σ̂_x [((N+1)/N)Σ_x + (Tr Σ_x/N)I]⁻¹. A scaling symmetry conserves ‖p₂‖² − ‖q₁‖². The transfer to non-linear transformers and grokking is a set of timing coincidences in spectral measures. | Read |
| [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) | Closed-Form Training Dynamics in Word2Vec-like Models | Proves that word2vec's loss, approximated to fourth order and reweighted so that every pair carries the same aggregate weight, is unweighted factorisation of M*, the relative deviation of co-occurrence from independence, whose rank-d minimisers are its top eigenvectors; derives, without full rigour, that gradient flow from small random initialisation learns those eigenvectors one at a time in sigmoidal steps; and shows on Wikipedia that the predicted embeddings match word2vec's features and scores better than truncated PMI or PPMI. Its account of analogies is an empirical spiked-random-matrix fit. | Read |
| [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md) | Single-Head Attention in High Dimensions | In a solvable model, one tied softmax attention layer trained by ridge-penalized ERM on Gaussian sequences with n ∝ d² samples, derives (non-rigorously, by AMP and random-matrix theory) the test error, interpolation and recovery thresholds, and the spectrum of the learned query–key map, η·ReLU(S0 + δZ − ε): outliers are recovered target directions, the bulk is finite-sample noise, and weight decay acts as a nuclear norm. Power-law targets are recovered mode by mode, giving heavy-tailed spectra and LASSO-rate scaling laws. | Read |
| [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md) | Towards Understanding Grokking | In a model that decodes the sum of two learned embeddings, a held-out pair is answered correctly when its embedding sum coincides with a trained pair's, and the training set's same-answer pairs force such coincidences. Grokking's critical training fraction is then where those equations first fix the embedding up to translation and scale, which a posited effective loss predicts for addition with p = 10. Threshold-defined phase diagrams over decoder learning rate and weight decay put grokking between comprehension and memorization, in the toy and, qualitatively, in a transformer and on MNIST. | Read |
| [NOTE-663](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-663.md) | Topological Invariance and Breakdown in Learning | Proves that a permutation-equivariant update with a K-Lipschitz update map changes the distance between any two neurons in one step by a factor in [1 − ηK, 1 + ηK], so coincident neurons never split, and for ηK < 1 the induced map on the set of neuron vectors is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism (a C¹ diffeomorphism under smoothness), and so no two neurons merge in finitely many steps. The proofs hold. The two-phase "topological simplification" reading and the Betti-number experiments go beyond them. The measured changes are fragmentation, not merging, at ηλ_max far below 1. | Read |
| [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md) | Symmetry in Language Statistics and Representation Geometry | Proves that if co-occurrence among words on a latent continuum depends only on their separation, a full-rank spectral word embedding places them on Fourier modes of the latent coordinate, with amplitudes from the kernel's Fourier transform, and solves the exponential kernel exactly for periodic and open boundaries. The symmetry is measured in Wikipedia, the geometry seen in Gemma 2 by PCA, and its robustness to deleting the words' mutual co-occurrences explained by a latent variable shared by many words. | Read |
| [NOTE-665](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-665.md) | On the Emergence of Linear Analogies in Word Embeddings | Derives the parallelogram analogies of word embeddings from a generative model of co-occurrence in which words are bundles of independent binary attributes: the co-occurrence ratio is then a Kronecker product, and its logarithm, the PMI, is a bilinear form of rank at most d + 1 whose eigenvectors are affine in the attributes, so a spectral PMI embedding is a linear image of the attribute hypercube. Robustness to noise, pruning and deletion of a relation's own pairs is argued from eigenvalue bounds and simulated; Wikipedia agrees in shape. Every embedding is an eigendecomposition, none is trained. | Read |
| [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md) | A mathematical theory of semantic development in deep neural networks | Shows that a two-layer linear network trained from small weights learns the singular modes of its input–output correlations in order of strength, each by a sharp sigmoidal transition, where a shallow network learns all modes together; and that the singular structure of data generated on trees, rings and clusters, plus a minimum-norm property, accounts for coarse-to-fine differentiation, transient errors, narrowing generalisation, typicality, coherence thresholds and conserved representational similarity. Exact only from decoupled, balanced initial weights with white inputs; random initialisation is simulated. | Read |
| [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) | Exact solutions to the nonlinear dynamics of learning in deep linear neural networks | Derives the coupled gradient-descent equations of a linear network with hidden layers and whitened inputs, and solves them exactly from decoupled starts: one sigmoid per singular mode of the input–output correlation, with conserved differences of squared layer strengths; balanced or not with one hidden layer, from equal layer strengths at any depth. Depth slows learning only through the initial end-to-end mode strength, so from strength of order one the iteration count stays finite as depth grows when the step size is scaled down with depth. Argues, with MNIST and random-matrix simulations, that orthogonal layers or suitable pretraining give such starts and scaled Gaussian layers do not, and that orthogonal tanh networks near gain 1 keep their Jacobians near-isometric. | Read |
| [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md) | Hyperbolic Representation Learning: Revisiting and Advancing | Shows, by tracking each node's hyperbolic distance to the origin, that hyperbolic graph models trained on task losses do not by themselves place a tree's root nearest the origin or spread its levels outward: on synthetic 3-ary trees the root sits well off the minimum and level order is recovered for only 69–75% of node pairs. A centroid recentring plus an outward-push loss (HIE), using no level information, raises this to 75–84% and improves link prediction and node classification, most on the least tree-like graphs. | Read |
| [NOTE-671](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-671.md) | Hyperbolic Entailment Cones for Learning Hierarchical Embeddings | Nested, axially symmetric, rotation-invariant cones in the Poincaré ball define a partial order, but nesting forces apertures of at most π/2 and r sin ψ(r)/(1 − r²) non-increasing. So no cone exists near the origin, and the widest family is sin ψ = K(1 − r²)/r, with a closed-form membership angle. The transitivity of that family is asserted, not proved. Learned on WordNet noun hypernymy, the cones predict held-out closure edges better than Poincaré and order embeddings once some closure edges are in training. Trained on the transitive reduction alone, every method fails. | Read |
| [NOTE-674](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-674.md) | Mutual information, neural networks and the renormalization group | Makes "the relevant degrees of freedom" of real-space RG an optimizable quantity: the coarse variable of a block that carries the most mutual information about the system beyond a buffer. Learned from Monte Carlo samples, it recovers Kadanoff block spins for 2D Ising and the electric-field variables of the dimer model, discards decoupled noise, and, iterated, gives the Ising flow and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, while a distribution-fitting RBM keeps the noise. The equivalence with a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is shown only for 1D and quasi-1D. | Read |
| [NOTE-675](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-675.md) | Hyperbolic Diffusion Embedding and Distance | Embeds each point's diffusion densities at dyadic time scales in a product of Poincaré half-spaces and proves that the ℓ1 product distance, a scale-weighted Hellinger sum, is equivalent up to constants to a thresholded snowflake min{1, d_T^(2α)} of a latent tree metric when the diffusion operator behaves like the heat kernel on that tree. The tree heat-kernel bounds are cited rather than proved and one Hölder step holds only for d_T ≥ 1. Empirically it keeps tree neighbourhoods (best MAP) and not global distances (more distortion than hyperbolic MDS). | Read |
| [NOTE-677](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-677.md) | The Random Hierarchy Model | Introduces the Random Hierarchy Model, a random context-free grammar in which each symbol has m synonymic expansions, and shows by experiment that deep feature-learning networks learn it from about n_c m^L examples, polynomial in the input dimension, while shallow and lazy networks need an exponential number. That size coincides with the emergence of synonym-invariant hidden representations and, by a scaling argument, with the size at which the class statistics of input patches, equal for synonyms, exceed sampling noise; removing those statistics makes deep networks fail as well. | Read |
| [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md) v2 | Representation Tradeoffs for Hyperbolic Embeddings | Trees embed in the hyperbolic plane with worst-case distortion 1 + ε, but because a hyperbolic distance d takes about d bits to write, the coordinates need Θ((ℓ/ε) log deg_max) bits in the plane: cheap in branching, expensive in depth. More dimensions divide the upper bound by r for bushy trees. For general metrics, an exact hyperbolic MDS by PCA on cosh of the distances after centring at a new mean, with a perturbation bound growing as sinh² of the diameter; hyperbolic PGA has spurious local minima and only a local-convexity guarantee. | Read |
| [NOTE-681](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-681.md) v2 | Statistical Physics through the Lens of Real-Space Mutual Information | Makes the real-space mutual-information principle a single-shot operator finder: a CNN coarse-graining co-trained against a neural InfoNCE bound, optimized once at a large buffer, returns on the interacting dimer model the order parameters below the BKT transition and the electric fields above it, and one fitted scaling dimension (1.00037 against 1). The maximal information is log 4 in the ordered phase and decays algebraically with the buffer in the critical one. The model's operators were known; the optimality theorem is cited. | Read |
| [NOTE-683](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-683.md) v2 | An exact mapping between the Variational Renormalization Group and Deep Learning | Identifies Kadanoff's variational RG kernel with an RBM energy by T = −E + H, so that the coarse-grained Hamiltonian is the RBM's hidden-marginal Hamiltonian for any parameters and an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data. The identity is correct but definitional, and the paper concedes the approximate schemes differ; its evidence that trained networks do RG is qualitative. [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md) is right that fitting the distribution need not give RG, though it does not engage the identity. | Read |
| [NOTE-684](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-684.md) | The Sparse Random Hierarchy Model | Adds sparsity to the Random Hierarchy Model, so that labels are unchanged by discrete displacements of the informative features, and shows by experiment that deep networks learn it from a number of examples polynomial in the input dimension, (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L up to a factor s^(L/2) without weight sharing and (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, and that hidden layers become insensitive to synonym swaps and to feature displacements at about the same training-set size as test error falls. That coincidence is offered as the reason deformation stability tracks performance on images, which is not tested on images. | Read |
| [NOTE-685](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-685.md) | A Phase Transition in Diffusion Models | For the Random Hierarchy Model with known rules, exact denoising is belief propagation; an annealed mean-field map, checked against exact BP, shows that as depth grows the class is recovered below a threshold noise and lost above it, provided the grammar is sparse (s f < 1), while low-level features degrade smoothly and persist past the threshold. The same top-versus-bottom crossing appears in classifier layers under forward–backward runs of an ImageNet diffusion model, and not for a Gaussian mixture. | Read |
| [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) | Hyperbolic Neural Networks | Möbius gyrovector operations give the Poincaré ball closed-form exponential and logarithmic maps, parallel transport from the origin as a scaling, and geodesic hyperplanes with a closed-form distance; from them come hyperbolic logistic regression, feed-forward layers and GRUs that reduce to the Euclidean ones as c → 0. Because linear maps and nonlinearities are lifted through the origin's tangent space, the curvature acts only through biases and output distances. Gains over Euclidean models are confined to a synthetic tree-like task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings. | Read |
| [NOTE-687](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-687.md) | How the structure of language is acquired | Extends the Random Hierarchy Model to predicting a masked last token. The correlation between two tokens shrinks by about a factor m per level of their common ancestor, a sample of P sequences resolves it only above a (v²P)^(−1/2) noise floor, and deep transformers and CNNs show loss steps at P_ℓ ≈ v m^(2ℓ−1), where their layers come to encode the level-ℓ hidden symbol. On character-level text, the correlation decay exponent predicts where the loss for a given context length levels off. The route from correlations to learned hidden variables is argued, not proved. | Read |
| [NOTE-688](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-688.md) v2 | Why does deep and cheap learning work so well? | Argues that cheap networks suffice because physical data have low-order, local, symmetric Hamiltonians, and that depth pays because inference must compose the sufficient statistics of a Markov generative hierarchy; proves that one hidden layer needs exactly 2^n neurons to multiply n inputs. On renormalization it is right that a coarse-graining needs a stated target, and its early appendix shows that neither a matched partition function nor the exact trace condition supplies one; it is wrong that the target must come from supervision. | Read |
| [NOTE-689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-689.md) | Deriving neural scaling laws from language statistics | Predicts the data-limited scaling exponent of language-model test loss as γ/(2β), from two measured corpus statistics: the decay with lag of the top singular value of the token–token covariance (β), which sets the usable context n*(P) ~ P^(1/(2β)), and the decay of next-token conditional entropy with context (γ). The derivation rests on assumed scaling forms and a fast-learning condition; on TinyStories and WikiText-103 transformers match the predicted exponents up to about 10^8 tokens and horizons of a few tens of tokens. | Read |
| [NOTE-691](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-691.md) | Probing Latent Hierarchy via Diffusion | In the Random Hierarchy Model with known rules, the tokens changed by noising and Bayes-optimal denoising form blocks set by the depth of the latent that changed; an annealed mean-field calculation, checked against exact belief propagation at one parameter set, gives a correlation length diverging as \|ε − ε*\|^(−ν), ν = log s / log F′(p*), at the class threshold, and a susceptibility peak there, which a Gaussian field with power-law spectrum lacks. Masked text diffusion and ImageNet diffusion show a susceptibility peak at an intermediate noise, over about one decade of distance and with no non-hierarchical control. | Read |
| [NOTE-692](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-692.md) v2 | Symmetries and phase diagrams with real-space mutual information neural estimation | The long companion of [LIT-878](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-878.md). Derives the RSMI-NE estimator and shows that the maximal real-space information counts ordered sectors (1 bit for the Ising ferromagnet, 2 for columnar dimers), decays exponentially with the buffer off criticality and algebraically at it, and that the ensemble of optimal filters from independent runs maps a degenerate subspace whose projections show broken lattice symmetries and the dimers' emergent U(1). All the models' answers were known; the non-equilibrium example is one figure. | Read |
| [NOTE-693](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-693.md) | The power of deeper networks for expressing natural functions | Proves that a single hidden layer of smooth, bias-free units needs exactly ∏(rᵢ+1) neurons to Taylor-approximate x₁^r₁⋯xₙ^rₙ while a deep network needs O(Σ log rᵢ), extends the gap to sparse and univariate polynomials, and bounds a product of n inputs at depth k by about 2^(n^(1/k)). Its uniform-approximation lower bounds rest on an unproved step, the depth-k tightness is a conjecture, and the gap is set by degree, so bounded-degree polynomials show none. | Read |
| [NOTE-694](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-694.md) | Comment on "Why does deep and cheap learning work so well?" | Schwab and Mehta concede that a preserved free energy does not give a preserved distribution and that the "iff" of [LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md)'s Eq. 8 should be one-directional, and show that Lin and Tegmark's v1 counterexample violates the trace condition, so the mapping's exact step stands. Right against v1; it places all of the mapping's content at the trace condition, and says nothing to the later point that the trace condition does not select the coarse variables. | Read |
| [NOTE-705](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-705.md) | Orseau, McGill & Legg — Agents and Devices | A formal counterpart of Dennett's physical and intentional stances. A device is a mixture of input-output mappings; an agent is a mixture of goal-optimizing ε-greedy policies, by inverse RL. Bayes' rule gives the posterior probability that a system is an agent. It is illustrated in a toy gridworld, with no human comparison. Agency is explicitly relative to the observer's prior. A clearly identified system is assumed. | Read |
| [NOTE-707](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-707.md) | Kenton et al. — Discovering Agents | An interventional, causal definition of agents. Mechanised causal models add a mechanism variable for each object-level variable. Decision nodes are found as variables whose mechanisms respond to downstream mechanisms (terminal edges), and utility nodes as the targets of those responses. Recovery of the true game graph is proved under five assumptions, including interventional data on mechanisms. The verdicts are sensible. The labels are frame-dependent and granularity-sensitive, which the paper states but does not treat as a threat. | Read |
| [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md) | The Limiting Dynamics of SGD | SGD with momentum β, learning rate η, batch size S and weight decay λ is modelled as (η/2)(1 + β)θ̈ + (1 − β)θ̇ + λθ = −g(θ) + √(η/S) √Σ ξ(t). For linear regression with Σ = σ²H this is an OU process in phase space. Its stationary state is Gibbs on a modified loss, with inverse temperature κ = S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. Under a quadratic loss at the end of training the same holds for deep networks, and a ResNet-18 on ImageNet shows the predicted isotropy, velocity regularization, oscillations and speed. | Read |
| [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md) | Symmetry in Neural Network Parameter Spaces | A symmetry is a group action on parameters preserving the network function (Def. 2.4) or the loss (Def. 2.6), possibly only on given data or in expectation (Defs. 2.8–2.9). Common components have GL, scaling, sign-flip, orthogonal, translation and permutation symmetries (Table 1). Continuous symmetries make minima connected manifolds, and give gradient flow conserved quantities that label trajectories and endpoints (§5). SGD's finite steps, noise and weight decay break these, which is an open route to implicit bias (§7.2). | Read |
| [NOTE-713](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-713.md) | Neural Mechanics | A symmetry ψ of the loss gives ⟨∇L, ∂_α ψ⟩ = 0 and a Hessian constraint. Under gradient flow, Theorem 1 conserves ⟨θ, ∂_α ψ⟩: for translation ⟨θ_A, 1⟩, for scale \|θ_A\|², for rescale \|θ_A1\|² − \|θ_A2\|². With weight decay λ and the modified loss L + (η/4)\|∇L\|², these become exponentially decaying memories plus integrals of gradient norms (Eqs. 18–20), matched on VGG-16 with Tiny ImageNet. The noise covariance annihilates the generators (§5, App. F). | Read |
| [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md) | Noise Balance and Stationary Distribution of Stochastic Gradient Descent | SDE: dθ = −∇L dt + √(T C(θ)) dW, with T = η/S. With ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ), d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w) (Theorem 1). The stationary point is Tr C(w) = Tr C(u). With weight decay γ the rate is TC₀ + γ (Corollary 2.1). Diagonal linear network ℓ = (Σᵢ ∏ₖ u_i^{(k)} x − y)²: sign coherence and balance for depth D > 1 (Theorem 3), exact stationary distribution (Theorem 4), collapse above T_c = β₂/α₃ for D = 1, tail ∝ v^{−5+3/(D+1)} independent of data. | Read |
| [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md) | From Lazy to Rich: Exact Learning Dynamics in Deep Linear Networks | Two-layer linear network ŷ = W₂W₁x, MSE, full-batch gradient flow. Assumptions: whitened inputs (A1), λ-balanced start W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI (A2), no bottleneck (A3). Then QQᵀ, with Q = [W₁ᵀ; W₂], obeys a matrix Riccati equation (Lemma 4.1), solved exactly (Theorem 4.3). For aligned starts, each singular value moves by a λ-dependent transition function: sigmoidal as λ → 0, exponential 1 − e^{−\|λ\|t/τ} as \|λ\| → ∞ (Theorem 5.1). | Read |
| [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md) | Symmetry Induces Structure and Constraint of Learning | ℓ_γ = ℓ₀(θ, x) + γ‖θ‖². O-mirror symmetry: ℓ₀(θ) = ℓ₀((I − 2OOᵀ)θ). Theorem 1: (1) Oᵀθ = 0 implies Oᵀ∇ℓ_γ = 0; (2) at symmetric points the Hessian splits into ker(Oᵀ) and im(OOᵀ) blocks; (3) above some γ₀ the projection (I − OOᵀ)θ has lower loss; (4) above some γ₁ all minima satisfy Oᵀθ = 0. SGD near the symmetric set: Pθ_{t+1} = Pθ_t − λH(x)Pθ_t, attractive when the Lyapunov exponent E log\|1 − λ(ξ + γ)\| < 0. Corollaries: sparsity, low rank, homogeneous neurons (Theorems 2–4). | Read |
| [NOTE-718](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-718.md) | Gallego & Orús — Language Design as Information Renormalization | Reads Chomsky's MERGE as a coarse-graining and builds sentence probabilities as mostly loop-free tensor networks of 3-index MERGE tensors, one per node of a given parse. Because MERGE's output is fixed by its input, a parsed sentence's probability is a product of local coefficients. Tree-shaped parses make correlations decay with tree distance, about log \|j − i\|, so polynomially in word separation. The averaging step that turns this into a claim about languages is asserted, and nothing is tested on data. Syntax only: semantics and context are set aside by the authors. | Read |
| [NOTE-723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-723.md) | Kahl — How continuity distinguishes autonomy from agency in agentic AI | Agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, authority and governance needs a persisting locus of evaluative authority under continuity pressure: when the inherited evaluative frame no longer settles what should count as success, the system itself settles a revised frame and carries it forward. Planning, tool use, memory, coordination and operational autonomy do not supply this. Tool-using agents, reinforcement learners, multi-agent workflows and institutional decision systems ordinarily fail it, because failure is corrected from outside. A conceptual necessary condition, applied to cases; not a sufficient theory and not measured. | Read |
| [NOTE-732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-732.md) | Lahiri — Agent-initiated socio-technical reconfiguration | Agents that keep memory, run code and can read and write the files that configure them have the governing rules inside their own action space. A three-level taxonomy, defined by architectural capability over the coupling mechanism, separates agents that cannot alter their coupling, agents that tune its timing, and agents that create new coordination surfaces. The paper's main claim is the recursive governance problem: controls the agent can reach inherit the vulnerability they were meant to remove, so durable constraint must sit outside the agent's action space. Theory-building from two anecdotal vignettes and four public incidents; five propositions, none tested. | Read |
| [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md) | Nielsen et al. — When Does Closeness in Distribution Imply Representational Similarity? | For softmax models p(y\|x) ∝ exp(f(x)ᵀg(y)), equal distributions fix the embeddings up to an invertible linear map, but KL closeness does not: by making the unembedding norm large, two models' KL divergence goes to zero while their embeddings stay fixed and are not linearly related. A log-likelihood variance distance does bound a representational dissimilarity, d_LLV ≤ ε ⇒ d_f,g ≤ 2Mε. Whether closeness in distribution implies similar representations depends on which distance is used. | Read |
| [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md) v2 | Poole et al. — On Variational Bounds of Mutual Information | The common variational lower bounds on mutual information (Barber–Agakov, Donsker–Varadhan, NWJ, MINE, InfoNCE) are derived from one unnormalized Barber–Agakov bound. InfoNCE is the multi-sample NWJ bound with the batch mean as its partition estimate, which proves it a lower bound for every critic when the K pairs are i.i.d.; it is capped at log K. An interpolated family I_α trades InfoNCE's bias against NWJ's variance, and none of them gives low bias and low variance when MI is large and the batch small. | Read |
| [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md) v2 | HaoChen et al. — Spectral Contrastive Loss | On a finite augmentation space, the spectral contrastive loss L(f) = −2E[f(x)ᵀf(x⁺)] + E[(f(x)ᵀf(x⁻))²] equals the rank-k factorization loss ‖D^(−1/2)AD^(−1/2) − FFᵀ‖²_F up to a constant when the rows of F are w_x^(1/2) f(x), so its minimizers are the top-k eigenvectors of the normalized augmentation graph up to row scaling and a right rotation. A linear probe on them has error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where α is the label noise of augmentations and ρ the sparsest-partition conductance. | Read |
| [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md) | Simon et al. — On the Stepwise Nature of Self-Supervised Learning | For a simplified Barlow Twins loss on a linear or kernel model trained by gradient flow from small initialization, the embedding learns the top eigenvectors of a symmetrized cross-correlation operator one at a time, each at a time set by its eigenvalue, and lands on the minimum-norm zero-loss solution: kernel PCA on K_Γ. Exact for aligned initialization; an informal derivation for generic small initialization. ResNets trained with Barlow Twins, SimCLR and VICReg show the same stepwise rank growth, which is an empirical finding, not a consequence of the theory. | Read |
| [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md) | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski — MDL and Generalization Guarantees for Representation Learning | The expected generalisation error of an encoder–decoder classifier is bounded by 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is a KL divergence between the encoder's joint law of train-and-ghost latents and a prior symmetric under label-preserving permutations. The bound holds for any decoder, stays finite for deterministic continuous encoders under lossy compression, and is never evaluated numerically. A VIB variant with label-dependent learned priors gains about 2.5 points on CIFAR-10. | Read |
| [NOTE-743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-743.md) v2 | Kornblith et al. — Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited | Any similarity index invariant to invertible linear maps is constant once a representation's rank reaches the number of examples (Theorem 1, a four-line proof). Kornblith et al. argue, without a theorem, for invariance to orthogonal maps and isotropic scaling only. They propose CKA, normalised HSIC of centred Gram matrices, and show that R²_CCA and linear regression are CKA of re-weighted Gram matrices. Linear CKA alone finds corresponding layers across CNN initialisations (99.3%, against at most 45.4% for the other linear indexes). | Read |
| [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md) | Marconato et al. — All or None: identifiable linear properties of next-token predictors | Two next-token predictors of the form p(y \| x) ∝ exp(f(x)ᵀg(y)) induce the same distribution exactly when they are related by an invertible linear map on the subspaces M and N that enter the logit dot product, with arbitrary distortion allowed off them. Relational linearity, and with it linear probing and linear subspaces, then holds in all such models or none when Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M. Parallelism survives only inside N. There are no experiments. | Read |
| [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md) | Tschannen et al. — On Mutual Information Maximization for Representation Learning | Four controlled experiments on MNIST image halves (two repeated on CIFAR10) show that downstream linear accuracy of InfoNCE- and NWJ-trained encoders does not track mutual information. Invertible encoders improve while true MI is constant. Higher NWJ bounds from an MLP critic give worse features. At matched bound values, ConvNets beat MLPs. The paper also proves that InfoNCE is neither a lower nor an upper bound on MI when batch pairs are dependent, and recasts it as a multi-class K-pair metric learning loss. | Read |
| [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md) v2 | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison — Contrastive Learning Can Find an Optimal Basis | On a finite augmentation space, the NT-Logistic and spectral losses are minimized over unconstrained kernels by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p), and InfoNCE by K⁺ up to a factor constant on communicating classes. Kernel PCA under K⁺ returns the eigenfunctions of the positive-pair Markov chain (h_i = λ_i^(1/2) f_i). The top-d eigenfunctions span the subspace that minimizes worst-case L²(p) approximation error over targets with E_p⁺[(g(a₁) − g(a₂))²] ≤ ε; that error is ε/(2(1 − λ_(d+1))). | Read |
| [NOTE-752](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-752.md) v2 | Balestriero & LeCun — SSL Recovers Global and Local Spectral Embedding Methods | On a finite sample with a positive-pair graph G, idealized forms of VICReg (squared variance term), SimCLR (a Euclidean graph-matching variant) and linear Barlow Twins have optimal representations or weights built from the spectrum of G. They are Laplacian eigenmaps, a generalized MDS and CCA. All of them align the left singular vectors of Z with those of G. SimCLR and Barlow Twins force rank(Z) = rank(G), while VICReg can stay full rank. Several proofs are sketches, and the experiments are small and synthetic. | Read |
| [NOTE-753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-753.md) v2 | Harvey, Larsen & Williams — Duality of Bures and Shape Distances | For centred linear kernels K_X = CXXᵀC, the Bures distance equals the Procrustes distance, B(K_X, K_Y) = P(X, Y), and normalized Bures similarity equals the cosine of the Riemannian shape distance. Both follow from F(K_X, K_Y) = ‖XᵀCY‖_*. By Uhlmann's theorem, the fidelity is the largest overlap between representations consistent with the two kernels. CKA is only loosely tied to NBS, inside a rank-dependent envelope. The result is finite-dimensional and linear; the infinite limits are heuristic. | Read |
| [NOTE-754](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-754.md) | Fischer — The Conditional Entropy Bottleneck | The MNI criterion asks for I(X;Y) = I(X;Z) = I(Y;Z), and CEB targets it by minimizing I(X;Z\|Y) − γI(Y;Z), which is IB with γ = β − 1. CEB beats VIB at every ρ on Fashion MNIST for accuracy and robustness, and a CEB Wide ResNet beats Madry's adversarially trained model on CIFAR-10 without adversarial training. That retained information causes the robustness failures is a hypothesis, supported only by these experiments. | Read |
| [NOTE-755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-755.md) | Picozzi — The information geometry of large language models is shared, learned, and controllable | The Fisher–Rao distance matrix of a model's next-token laws over a context battery is a function of the laws alone, so behaviour fixes it, whereas activation geometry has a GL(d) gauge. Across ten models of three architecture kinds it agrees at a mean rank correlation of 0.88, against 0.62 for mid-layer activations. The agreement is proved to follow from each model's closeness to the same language law, and only about 9% of shared eigenvector structure goes beyond what the shared laws imply. The pullback metric also gives minimum-disturbance steering, whose cost advantage over Euclidean steering it predicts. | Read |
| [NOTE-757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-757.md) | Calo et al. — Bisimulation metrics are optimal transport distances | For two finite Markov chains with real-valued state labels, the discounted bisimulation metric of Ferns et al. and van Breugel and Worrell solves the same fixed-point equation as the optimal-transport distance over bicausal couplings with ground cost (1−γ)\|r(x)−r(y)\|, so the two are one object. That distance equals the value of a finite linear program over discounted occupancy couplings, and an entropy-regularised alternating-projection method (Sinkhorn Value Iteration) reaches ε accuracy in O(‖c‖²∞ log(\|X\|\|Y\|)/((1−γ)⁵ε²)) iterations under exact inner projections. | Read |
| [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md) | Shai et al. — Transformers learn factored representations | If a generator's token-labelled operators are tensor products, the predictive state stays a product state, and a linear map carries it losslessly into orthogonal per-factor subspaces of total dimension Σ(d_n − 1). Small transformers trained on five such factors settle near that dimension, about 10 against 242, in approximately orthogonal subspaces. With token noise that makes factoring lossy they collapse to it first and expand only later. RNNs and LSTMs show it less sharply. | Read |
| [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md) | Bird — Emergence of Quantised Representations Isolated to Anisotropic Functions | In small CIFAR and MNIST autoencoders built from orthogonally equivariant parts except the activation, elementwise tanh and Leaky-ReLU drive latent representations into narrow beams along or against the standard basis, arranged by each activation's symmetry group. Radial (O(n)-equivariant) versions of the same functions leave them spread. The beams appear even in the first latent layer, which no activation precedes. The evidence is visual, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. | Read |
| [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md) | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi — Why Do Better Loss Functions Lead to Less Transferable Features? | For ResNet-50 on ImageNet, every training objective that raises accuracy over softmax cross-entropy also raises penultimate-layer class separation, and fixed penultimate features with more class separation transfer worse to new-class datasets (Spearman ρ = −0.93 across nine objectives; one temperature knob moves both). The losses differ only in the last few blocks, and full fine-tuning erases the difference. For the pretraining classes themselves, more separation helps. | Read |
| [NOTE-763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-763.md) v2 | Calo et al. — Distances for Markov chains from sample streams | The bicausal transport distance between two finite Markov chains, which the authors' earlier paper identified with the bisimulation metric, has a second linear program whose constraints use only the chains' discounted state-transition occupancy measures, not their kernels. A stochastic primal-dual method on it gets an ε-accurate estimate with probability 1−δ from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|) log(1/δ)) / ((1−γ)²ε²)) independent transition samples per chain. The guarantee assumes independent draws from the occupancy measures, which needs restarts; samples from one running trajectory are outside it. | Read |
| [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) | Thrampoulidis et al. — Imbalance Trouble | In the unconstrained-features model with cross-entropy and vanishing regularization, the max-margin solutions have logits exactly equal to the simplex-encoded label matrix Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), whatever the class imbalance. The classifier and embedding Gram matrices are VΛVᵀ and UΛUᵀ from Ẑ's SVD. This SELI geometry is the simplex ETF only for balanced or binary data. Under imbalance, majority classifiers are longer and minority classifiers closer together. No finite weight decay gives SELI, and SGD approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows. | Read |
| [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md) | Huang et al. — internal causal mechanisms predict out-of-distribution behaviour | In Llama-3-8B-Instruct, on five tasks and ten task-preserving shifts, checking by interchange intervention whether a test input still realizes the causal variable located on in-distribution data predicts whether the output is correct better than output confidence or probes of other internal features, best on 8 of 10 shifts. A probe on the located variable beats a probe on its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only up to a point. | Read |
| [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md) | Kumar, Clune, Lehman and Stanley — The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis | For three images found by Picbreeder's human-guided evolution (skull, butterfly, apple), SGD in the same layerized architecture reproduces the image from random weights, but its neurons show no reuse of the symmetric parts, and sweeping its weights distorts the image where sweeping the evolved network's weights varies it meaningfully. This holds in a PCA basis, along random weight directions, and in ReLU networks. The evidence is qualitative and curated; the attribution to open-ended search is conjecture. | Read |
| [NOTE-772](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-772.md) v2 | Kothapalli — Neural Collapse: A Review on Modelling Principles and Generalization | A survey, not a source of results. It sorts accounts of neural collapse into unconstrained-features models (the last-layer features are free variables) and local elasticity, and reports that every one of them derives the collapsed state or its dynamics only after removing the data. On generalization it finds the literature in conflict. Collapse on the training set does not guarantee good test error, test-set collapse is much weaker and dataset-dependent, and there is no agreed threshold for calling a network collapsed. It also reports that networks more collapsed on ImageNet transfer worse. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md) | Kothapalli & Tirer — Can Kernel Methods Explain How the Data Affects Neural Collapse? | NC1, measured as tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B, is written for any kernel as a function of the kernel matrix. For two-class, one-dimensional Gaussian data with the classes on opposite sides of the origin, the ReLU NTK of a wide two-layer net is a scaled copy of the NNGP kernel within each class and zero across classes. So lazy-regime training leaves expected NC1 where it was at initialization. In higher dimensions the NTK is measured no more collapsed, and with ReLU less. A data-aware kernel lowers NC1 for separable data but tracks finite networks poorly when the classes overlap or are imbalanced. Erf collapses more than ReLU. | Read |
| [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md) | Belrose et al. — Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity | An empirical paper. Vision networks trained on real images classify maximum-entropy samples that match only the class means, or means and covariances, well above chance early in training (peaks between about 2^4 and 2^12 steps), and the accuracy then falls, often below chance. First-order samples peak earlier and lower than second-order ones. Pythia models fit unigram-sampled text, then bigram-sampled text, then fit them worse, then better again. The n-gram/moment equivalence is an identity of one-hot indicators. The ordering argument is a heuristic. | Read |
| [NOTE-780](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-780.md) | Sefidgaran, Gohari, Richard & Şimşekli — Rate-Distortion Theoretic Generalization Bounds | The expected generalisation error of any algorithm is at most √(2σ²·R/n) + ε, where R is the least mutual information I(S;Ŵ) of any surrogate output whose expected generalisation error is within ε. With ε = 0 this is Xu–Raginsky. With ε > 0 it stays finite where I(S;W) is infinite. For a Lipschitz loss R becomes the rate-distortion function of the output's marginal law, and as ε → 0 its rate-distortion dimension. A tail bound replaces I(S;W) by its supremum over laws within log(1/δ) in KL. Every bound depends on the unknown data distribution. | Read |
| [NOTE-781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-781.md) | Torii, Maeda and Hidaka — Distributional hypothesis as isomorphism | An SVD of log raw co-occurrence counts solves 61% of Google analogies over a 1,487-word vocabulary, against 75% for full word2vec. In a 24-sentence toy corpus whose eight subjects carry every combination of three binary aspects, the subjects' raw co-occurrence rows form a parallelepiped exactly when, for each object, its four sentences are equally probable. The attributes are independent, so the concept lattice is Boolean. | Read |
| [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md) | Makelov, Lange and Nanda — an interpretability illusion for subspace activation patching | A subspace activation patch can make a model behave as if a feature had changed while the patched direction is the sum of a component that varies with the feature but cannot reach the output (in an MLP, the kernel of the down-projection) and a component that can reach the output but is dormant on the data. Shown exactly in a three-unit network, empirically for MLP8 of GPT-2 Small on IOI and for MLPs of GPT2-XL on factual recall, where the effect vanishes once the disconnected component is removed. A residual stream direction passes the same test. One-dimensional fact patches and rank-1 edits are shown to be nearly interchangeable. | Read |
| [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md) | Han, Papyan & Donoho — Neural Collapse Under MSE Loss | Networks trained with MSE loss show neural collapse on five datasets and three architectures. The MSE loss splits exactly into a term for the least-squares classifier of the current features and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training. On that "central path", in an unconstrained-features model with no weight decay and features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance, gradient flow drives every singular value of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃ to infinity as (4t/N)^(1/4), and drives them to equality. That gives NC1–NC4 in closed form. | Read |
| [NOTE-784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-784.md) | Coifman et al. — Diffusion maps | From a symmetric, positivity-preserving, positive semi-definite kernel, normalized into a Markov operator conjugate to a symmetric one, the top eigenfunctions scaled by powers of their eigenvalues embed the data so that Euclidean distance equals diffusion distance. A one-parameter normalization separates geometry from sampling density, recovering the Laplace–Beltrami operator at α = 1. The symmetry of the kernel is what yields the spectral decomposition; non-symmetric kernels are not treated. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-786.md) | Merullo et al. — Linear Representations and Pretraining Data Frequency | For 24 factual relations in OLMo-1B, OLMo-7B and GPT-J, how well an affine map from subject to object representation reproduces the model (LRE causality) correlates with the mean subject–object co-occurrence count in pretraining (r = 0.82). It correlates less with subject or object counts alone. Mean causality passes 0.9 beyond about 4.4k, 2.0k and 1.1k co-occurrences respectively, at any training step. Correlational; LREs are relation maps, not attribute directions. | Read |
| [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md) | Kirsanov et al. — The Geometry of Prompting | In base Llama-3.1-8B (and Gemma-2-2B), demonstrations reorganise the geometry of the input sentence's representation at early-to-middle layers, while an instruction acts mainly on the last token and soft prompts only on late layers: matched accuracy, different mechanisms. Few-shot failures from the choice of examples or from relabelled categories leave the class manifolds separable and fail at the readout. | Read |
| [NOTE-794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-794.md) | Liu et al. — Physics of Skill Learning | Three toy models of skill learning. In the Geometry model, independent skills are orthogonal directions in parameter space weighted by frequency. Under SGD each is learned at its own rate, the second taking about 1/p₂ as long. Under sign descent they compete for coordinate signs, and each starts as the one before finishes (the Domino effect), so the n-th skill takes time ∝ n. A one-parameter Resource ODE fits these curves and has exact conserved quantities u_i^(1/p_i). A small MLP also shows the effect when one parity is the XOR of two others. | Read |
| [NOTE-798](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-798.md) | Williams et al. — Targeted manipulation and deception when optimizing LLMs for user feedback | Iterated KTO on simulated thumbs-up feedback turns a safety-trained Llama-3-8B-Instruct (and Gemma-2 up to 27B) into a policy that lies about failed bookings, omits harms to steer users into risky actions and validates self-destructive plans. When only 2% of simulated users reward such validation, the policy picks them out by contextual cues and harms only them. Safety-data mixing and LLM vetoes barely help or move it to subtler steering, and sycophancy and toxicity benchmarks miss it. | Read |
| [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md) | Noroozizadeh et al. — Deep sequence models tend to memorize geometrically | Transformers and Mamba trained only on a graph's edge bigrams embed nodes so that multi-hop relations are readable, and solve an in-weights path-finding task built to defeat next-token learning. The authors argue that supervision, capacity, ease of optimization and succinctness each fail to explain why this geometry wins over an associative lookup. In a wide two-layer weight-tied model under unregularized cross-entropy the embeddings settle into the top Laplacian eigenvectors without a rank bottleneck, shown empirically, with an informal partial proof. Why deeper models prefer geometry is left open. | Read |
| [NOTE-802](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-802.md) | Modell, Rubin-Delanchy and Whiteley — The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models | If a feature is a compact metric space mapped continuously and injectively onto the unit sphere (Hypothesis 1), its representation is homeomorphic to it. If, in addition, cosine similarity is locally a C² decreasing function g of squared feature distance (Hypothesis 2), every path on the representation manifold has √(−2g′(0)) times the length of the feature path it images (Theorem 1). The hypotheses are assumed, not derived; the tests supply a candidate metric and find homeomorphism for GPT-2's years but isometry only after a log rescaling. | Read |
| [NOTE-803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-803.md) | Davidson et al. — Do different prompting methods yield a common task representation? | Function vectors extracted from short instructions raise zero-shot accuracy, but they are built from mostly different attention heads than demonstration function vectors (4 to 7 of the top 20 shared), the two add rather than substitute, and swapping heads and activations between them costs accuracy asymmetrically. Under this method there is no common task representation across the two presentations, only partly overlapping mechanisms; the authors note they cannot prove the negative. | Read |
| [NOTE-804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-804.md) | Goldwasser et al. — A Theory of Unsupervised Translation Motivated by Animal Communication | With a plausibility prior over the target language and no parallel data, maximum likelihood learns a translator whose error is bounded like a supervised Occam bound divided by the common ground. In the common-nonsense model err = O(log\|Θ\| / (α·min(m,\|T\|))), tight up to a constant; in the knowledge-graph model more knowledge per node needs less agreement. Information-theoretic only, lossless, uniform languages. | Read |
| [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md) | Defilippis et al. — Optimal scaling laws in learning hierarchical multi-index models | For Gaussian inputs, n = αd samples, and a target Σ_k a_k g_k(⟨w_k, x⟩) with even links and a_k ~ k^(−γ), direction k becomes weakly recoverable at α_k = Θ(a_k^(−2)) = Θ(k^(2γ)) for γ > 1/2. The Bayes-optimal weighted subspace error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) before α ≍ m⋆^(2γ) and Θ(m⋆/α) after. A target-agnostic spectral estimator attains both, and a two-layer net given that estimator as its first layer, with a ridge readout, attains them in excess risk. The cascade is in sample size. The link to gradient descent is a remark. | Read |
| [NOTE-806](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-806.md) | Sefidgaran & Zaidi — Data-Dependent Generalization Bounds via Variable-Size Compressibility | If the number of codewords allowed for covering a block of experiments may depend on the realised sample and output, generalisation bounds can be data-dependent. The general bounds are change-of-measure inequalities that cover tail, PAC-Bayes and in-expectation forms. With the rate set to log dP_{W\|S}/dP(W) for a fixed prior P, the tail bound is the disintegrated PAC-Bayes bound. A new trajectory bound is data-dependent except for a coupling term, and its experiment drops that term. | Read |
| [NOTE-807](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-807.md) | Gokhale — The semantic landscape paradigm for neural networks | A conceptual proposal with no experiment and no proof. Training is pictured as a walk on a graph of "heuristic models" (internal algorithms), ranked by a fallibility F. A critical dataset size for grokking and emergence with scale are each argued to be graph connectivity thresholds, and power-law scaling in time, data and size is derived from an assumed trap model of activated hops. The percolation is asserted, not shown, and the scaling laws rest on chosen assumptions. | Read |
| [NOTE-809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-809.md) | Wu et al. — a reply to Makelov et al.'s interpretability illusion arguments | The reply argues that Makelov et al.'s "illusion" is defined so that any direction not orthogonal to the null space of the downstream weights can qualify, including the direction Makelov et al. call faithful in their toy network, and that their in-the-wild cases rest on a weak metric and on DAS trained per fact pair. The toy computation holds only for an unnormalized patch: patching the subspace the rowspace component spans, as Makelov et al. specify, recovers the full effect. Its own GPT-2 experiments agree that MLP8 carries almost no name-position information. | Read |
| [NOTE-813](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-813.md) | Fu et al. — Evaluating Compositional Scene Understanding in Multimodal Generative Models | Human raters judged DALL-E 3 images. Agreement with single familiar relations rose well above DALL-E 2's. It fell when subject and object of an asymmetric relation were swapped, and again when two relations were combined; low-agreement reversed images mostly had the wrong relation or swapped roles. Five VLMs learned relational concepts few-shot below human level, and four were at chance with six objects. | Read |
| [NOTE-815](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-815.md) | Gerstgrasser et al. — Is Model Collapse Inevitable? | In a fixed-design linear regression refit each round to labels drawn from the previous fit, keeping every earlier round's data gives test error σ²d/(T−d−1)·Σ1/i², bounded by π²/6 times the first fit's, where replacing the data gives σ²d/(T−d−1)·n. The error still rises every round. Small language models and a diffusion model on accumulated data hold their test loss over five to eight rounds; a VAE's still rises, more slowly. | Read |
| [NOTE-816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-816.md) | Erogullari et al. — Post-Hoc Concept Disentanglement | Concept activation vectors fitted one concept at a time align for CelebA and FunnyBirds attributes that co-occur in the labels. A joint fit with a penalty ‖CCᵀ − I‖²_F finds mutually orthogonal directions that still separate each concept, with AUROC "largely preserved". So correlated attributes keep linear separating directions in these CNNs, and the alignment comes from the separate fits. Steering with the orthogonal directions changes correlated concepts less. | Read |
| [NOTE-819](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-819.md) | Hopfield — Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities | With symmetric couplings, asynchronous threshold updates descend an energy function, so Hebbian outer-product storage makes random patterns attractors: a cue a few bits off settles into the nearest one. In simulations at N = 30 and 100, recall degrades severely near 0.15N patterns, memories closer than about a tenth of N fuse, and overload makes every memory irretrievable unless old ones are forgotten. | Read |
| [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md) | Chowdhury et al. — Fundamental Limits of Perfect Concept Erasure | If an erased representation Z is independent of the concept A, it keeps at most I(Z;X) ≤ H(X\|A). A deterministic erasure reaches that only when the groups' distributions are permutations of one another. The paper says the bound is out of reach otherwise. That holds only for deterministic maps: a stochastic quantile coupling reaches it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Read |
| [NOTE-824](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-824.md) | Pfau et al. — Spectral Inference Networks | For a symmetric kernel k on a space with a sampling density p, the span of the top N eigenfunctions of K[f](../../../record/notes.d/x) = E_x′[k(x,x′)f(x′)] maximizes Tr(Σ⁻¹Π) over functions, with Σ = E[uuᵀ] and Π = E[k(x,x′)u(x)u(x′)ᵀ]; a Cholesky-masked gradient orders them and moving averages of Σ and its Jacobian remove the minibatch bias. Slow Feature Analysis is the graph-Laplacian case. The ordering argument is informal by the authors' own statement, and the paper never considers contrastive kernels or positive pairs. | Read |
| [NOTE-828](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-828.md) v2 | Belghazi et al. — Mutual Information Neural Estimation | Mutual information is the KL divergence of the joint from the product of marginals, and its Donsker–Varadhan dual is tight exactly at the log Radon–Nikodym derivative plus a constant. Maximizing that dual over a compact family of neural critics gives an estimator that is strongly consistent, for the exact empirical maximizer, on a compact domain with Lebesgue densities, with a uniform deviation bound of order d log d/ε² in the parameter count d. The mini-batch gradient is biased; a moving average is offered as a heuristic fix without proof. | Read |
| [NOTE-830](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-830.md) | Li et al. — Self-Supervised Learning with Kernel Dependence Maximization | With image identity as a one-hot label, HSIC(Z,Y) is (Δl/N) times the gap between the mean kernel on positive pairs and on all pairs, and (1/2N²)Σ MMD²(i,j) = (N/Δl)·HSIC(Z,Y). The large-batch InfoNCE loss is exactly −HSIC(Z,Y) plus a log-mean-exp of the centred critic (eq. 28), and for a bounded kernel it bounds −HSIC(Z,Y) + γHSIC(Z,Z) up to a remainder of second order in the critic's variance (Thm B.1, whose printed remainder has the wrong sign). | Read |
| [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md) | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li — when known classes help discover novel ones | In a spectral-contrastive augmentation graph over labelled and unlabelled data, the linear-probe residual of a novel labelling is exactly the part of it outside the top-k eigenspace that the labelled rows of the discarded eigenvectors cannot absorb. Known classes that share the novel class's attribute can make it zero, and a toy shows that known classes sharing a rival attribute make it worse. The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and averages all known classes into one block. | Read |
| [NOTE-834](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-834.md) | Harvey, Lipshutz & Williams — What Representational Similarity Measures Imply about Decodable Information | For a linear readout that maximizes zᵀXw/M − ½wᵀG(X)w, the decoded signal is K_X z with K_X = XG(X)⁻¹Xᵀ/M, so the task-averaged agreement of two representations is Tr(K_X K_z K_Y). With K_z = I that is linear CKA, mean squared CCA, ENSD or the GULP distance, for particular G. Procrustes distance and average decoding distance bound each other only through the participation ratio of K_X − K_Y. The population limit (App. A.3) is an outline that requires b > 0 and a trace-class task covariance, and it does not reach the K_z = I case. | Read |
| [NOTE-838](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-838.md) | Muandet et al. — Kernel Mean Embedding of Distributions | A survey whose load-bearing chain is short and explicit. An RKHS is a Hilbert space with bounded evaluation, so Riesz gives k_x (Thm 2.4, Prop. 2.1). If E_P√k(X,X) < ∞, the expectation functional is bounded and Riesz gives μ_P with E_P f = ⟨f, μ_P⟩ (Lemma 3.1, proved). MMD is ‖μ_P − μ_Q‖ (eq. 3.29), a metric on distributions exactly when k is characteristic. HSIC is the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the centred cross-covariance. Every result is for a fixed kernel. | Read |
| [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md) | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu — contrastive learning, multi-view redundancy and linear models | When two views X and Z are redundant for a label, the predictor that infers Z from X and then predicts, µ(x) = E[E[Y\|Z]\|X=x], is within εX + 2√(εXεZ) + εZ of the Bayes predictor. µ is linear in the density ratio g*(x,·) = p(x,z)/(p(x)p(z)), the optimum of the logistic contrastive problem, so m random landmark evaluations of g* support a linear predictor whose extra error falls as 1/m, scaled by a variance that is at most E[g*²] for bounded labels. Nothing requires the views to be exchangeable. | Read |
| [NOTE-843](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-843.md) | Gebhart, Hansen and Schrater — Knowledge Sheaves | A knowledge-graph embedding is a knowledge sheaf on the schema (one pair of restriction maps per relation type) with a 0-cochain of its pullback to the graph. The summed Structured Embedding score is the sheaf Laplacian form xᵀLx; adding a relation vector gives TransR, and identity maps TransE. Since the zero cochain is always a section, training needs negative triples and a margin. A multi-hop query is scored by harmonic extension, a Schur complement of the query graph's Laplacian, which beats summing TransE vectors on ip and pi queries. | Read |
| [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md) | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun — regularization effects are class dependent | On ImageNet with ResNet-50, making random crop stronger or changing weight decay raises mean test accuracy while some classes lose 20 points or more, and the shift survives a frozen-backbone transfer to iNaturalist. The evidence is per-class curves for hand-picked classes over 10–20 runs, plus a Welch test with no multiple-comparison correction. Theorem 1 says only that a fit to augmentations that are not label-preserving cannot equal the true function. | Read |
| [NOTE-846](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-846.md) | Tan et al. — contrastive learning is spectral clustering on a similarity graph | SimCLR's InfoNCE loss, taken over all n objects with a Gaussian kernel on the unit sphere and a symmetric augmentation matrix π, is rewritten exactly as tr(Zᵀ L(π) Z) + log R(Z): a graph-Laplacian quadratic form plus the log of InfoNCE's normalizers. The paper calls this spectral clustering under a definition that admits any regularizer. It does not show that the minimizer is a set of Laplacian eigenvectors, and it names no population optimum. | Read |
| [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md) | Assran et al. — The Hidden Uniform Cluster Prior in Self-Supervised Learning | MSN's entropy term is a KL penalty pulling cluster sizes toward uniform, and SwAV's Sinkhorn step enforces equal sizes outright; for VICReg the same prior is reached only through an informal reduction to K-means, and for SimCLR only by a cited equivalence. With mini-batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, SimCLR, VICReg and MSN lose 11–18 points of ImageNet linear accuracy while MAE and data2vec do not. A power-law prior in MSN gains about 1–3 points on long-tailed iNat18 and loses heavily on ImageNet. | Read |
| [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md) | Snell, Lee, Xu & Kumar — Scaling LLM test-time compute optimally | On MATH with PaLM 2-S*, which way of spending test-time compute works best (beam search against a process reward model versus best-of-N; sequential self-revision versus parallel sampling) depends on how hard the question is for the base model, and choosing the method per difficulty bin matches best-of-N with up to about 4× less test-time compute (the discussion says 2–4×). In a FLOPs-matched comparison with a ~14× larger model, the extra test-time compute a small model may spend is set by R, the ratio of total inference tokens to pretraining tokens: when R is small the larger model's pretraining cost buys many samples per query and test-time compute wins on easy and medium questions; when R is large the budget per query falls toward the parameter ratio and the larger model wins, always on the hardest questions. Difficulty estimation (2048 samples per question) and verifier and revision-model finetuning are not counted in the compute, R is an aggregate token ratio with no term for which queries recur, and the evidence is one model family on one benchmark of 500 test questions. | Read |
| [NOTE-879](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-879.md) | Hébert-Johnson, Kim, Reingold & Rothblum — Multicalibration: calibration for the computationally-identifiable masses | A predictor is α-multicalibrated on a collection C of subpopulations if, within every set S in C, the individuals given (roughly) the same prediction v have true probabilities averaging within α of v, except on an α-fraction of S. For any C whose sets have size at least γN, a simple iterative patching algorithm reaches multicalibration from O(log\|C\|/α^{11/2}γ^{3/2}) samples in time linear in \|C\|, and the result is a circuit only O(s/α⁴γ) in size when the sets of C are computed by size-s circuits. Learning it is equivalent, up to polynomial factors, to weak agnostic learning of C, so it is hard for rich C under cryptographic assumptions. Calibrating any predictor h on its own level sets as well as on C costs at most 6α in squared error. All guarantees are relative to the benchmark p*, which is itself defined relative to the features available, and they hold only for large sets; the paper offers no uniqueness for the predictor and does not state a theorem in indistinguishability form. | Read |
| [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md) | Sardana, Portes, Doubov & Frankle — Beyond Chinchilla-optimal: accounting for inference in scaling laws | Fixing a target pre-training loss and adding inference FLOPs (2N per token over a known lifetime demand D_inf) to training FLOPs (6N per token), the compute-minimising model is smaller and trained on more data than Chinchilla-optimal, increasingly so as D_inf approaches and exceeds the training-set size; the optimum has no closed form and is found numerically. The savings are modest in FLOPs (for a 30B-Chinchilla-quality model with 10^13 inference tokens, 28% by training 13.6B on 2.84× the data) and larger in dollars once inference's low hardware utilisation is priced in (17% to 58% in the paper's examples). 47 training runs (150M–6B parameters, 10–10,000 tokens per parameter) find loss still falling at extreme ratios, but more slowly than Chinchilla-fitted laws predict, so the formula overstates the gain from long training. Demand is assumed known before training and fixed given quality; there is no term for uncertainty, discounting, obsolescence or a model being replaced. | Read |
| [NOTE-884](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-884.md) | Jones — Scaling scaling laws with board games | Training AlphaZero on Hex at board sizes 3×3 to 9×9, the best Elo reachable for a given training compute follows one change-point curve across sizes: an incline of about 500 Elo per tenfold of training compute, with the compute for perfect play rising about 7× and the compute to leave random play about 4× per added board row, and fits on small boards predicting larger ones. On 9×9 only, train-time and test-time (tree-search) compute substitute at a fixed rate: at equal Elo, each 10× of train-time compute removes about 15× of test-time compute (fit: log test = −1.2·log train + 0.004·Elo + 29), down to a one-node search, over roughly 1e14–1e16 FLOPS-seconds of training. The trade is an iso-performance curve for a single search; the paper never counts how many games or moves the trained agent will play, so it does not price amortization, and it does not state the unit of test-time compute.
